concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of intractable vomiting, postprandial upper abdominal pain, and bloating, combined with the finding of compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta, are consistent with Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome.
The patient's symptoms of intractable vomiting, bloating, and progressive inability to tolerate oral intake, combined with the finding of marked gastric distension, are consistent with Gastroparesis.

The patient's symptoms of intractable vomiting, postprandial upper abdominal pain, and bloating, combined with the finding of marked gastric distension, are consistent with Gastrointestinal Obstruction.

The patient's symptoms of intractable vomiting, postprandial upper abdominal pain, and bloating, combined with the finding of compression of the third portion of the duodenum, are consistent with Duodenal obstruction.
The patient's symptoms of postprandial upper abdominal pain and bloating, combined with the finding of normal upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, are consistent with Functional dyspepsia.
The patient's symptoms of intractable vomiting, postprandial upper abdominal pain, and bloating, combined with the finding of marked gastric distension, are consistent with Small bowel obstruction.

The patient's symptoms of intractable vomiting, postprandial upper abdominal pain, and bloating, combined with the finding of marked gastric distension, are consistent with Chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction.

The patient's symptoms of intractable vomiting, postprandial upper abdominal pain, and bloating, combined with the finding of marked gastric distension, are consistent with Gastric outlet obstruction.
It explains the finding of no intrinsic luminal lesions in the context of duodenal obstruction.
